---
description: "Rules for tests, fixtures and the golden-BOM eval suite in tests and evals: no network, determinism, fixture design, eval cases required for behavior changes."
applyTo: "{tests,evals,fixtures}/**"
---

# Testing and Evaluation Rules

## Absolute rules

- **No live network calls.** Not to suppliers, not to the LLM provider, not to
  anything. A test that needs the internet is a broken test.
- **No wall-clock dependence.** Inject time through `StageContext`. Tests that fail in
  a different timezone or at month boundaries are defects.
- Tests must pass when run in any order and in parallel.

## Test layers

| Layer | Location | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| Unit | `tests/unit/` | Pure functions: value parsing, derating math, price breaks |
| Stage | `tests/stages/` | One stage, fixture in → artifact out |
| Contract | `tests/contracts/` | Schema validity, migrations, adapter conformance |
| Pipeline | `tests/pipeline/` | Full run against fixture adapters |
| Eval | `evals/` | Golden BOMs with scored expectations |

## Fixture design

Fixtures must include the ugly cases, not just the clean ones. A fixture set that only
contains well-formed BOMs proves nothing about a tool whose whole job is messy input.

Required coverage in `fixtures/boms/`:

- One export per EDA tool: Altium, KiCad, Eagle/Fusion, OrCAD/Allegro
- Ad-hoc Excel with merged cells, a title block above the header row, and a trailing
  notes row
- Reference designator ranges (`R1-R8`), gaps, and duplicates across lines
- A quantity that disagrees with the reference designator count
- Values in mixed notation: `4k7`, `0.1uF`, `100n`, `10 kΩ ±1%`, `1R0`
- A DNP / "do not populate" line
- A row with a manufacturer part number and nothing else
- A row with a description and no parameters at all

Required coverage in `fixtures/catalogs/`:

- Zero stock with a quoted lead time
- Missing MOQ / SPQ
- Price breaks in a non-default currency
- NRND and obsolete lifecycle states
- One MPN offered by multiple manufacturers
- A part that passes every parameter but has the wrong footprint

## Determinism tests

Every stage has a test that runs it twice on the same input and asserts byte-identical
artifacts. Planning additionally asserts stable output across machines — sort keys
must be total, never dependent on insertion order.

## Golden-BOM evals

An eval case is a BOM plus expected outcomes:

```yaml
case: mixed_passives_v1
bom: fixtures/boms/mixed_passives.csv
snapshot: fixtures/catalogs/2026-09-eval-snapshot
expect:
  normalized_rows: 48
  unresolved_max: 2
  filled_at_tier_0_or_1_min: 44
  blocked_requirements: [R17]     # 0402 1% 25V where catalog only has 16V
  plan_modes: [lowest_cost, fastest_delivery, balanced]
  lowest_cost_total_eur: "41.87"
```

Any change to normalization, classification, policy, or planning behavior **requires a
new or updated eval case in the same change.** This is the only mechanism that keeps
prompt and rule tuning honest.

## Tracked metrics

Report these on every eval run and treat regressions as blocking:

- % of BOM rows normalized without LLM fallback
- % of requirements filled at substitution tier 0 or 1
- Count of `BLOCKING` issues
- Plan total delta versus the previous run for each decision mode

## Anti-patterns

- Asserting on LLM prose. Assert on structure, flags, and counts instead.
- Snapshot tests over whole artifacts with no assertion about why. Assert the fields
  that carry meaning.
- Fixtures generated by the code under test. Fixtures come from real exports, hand-
  checked once.
